newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly higher on Tuesday after a slow trading session during which prices hardly moved.
Dealers said trade was extremely thin as the market paused after the rally of the last couple of weeks, adding volumes might remain light if no new economic impulse emerged.
"I expect bond prices to hover within a relatively narrow range for a while until they break out (of the range) when we have some important news," one dealer said.
He said it was hard to say in which direction the market would move next as that depended on the nature of the news.
Short-dated bond prices were slightly under pressure, with the 6.25 percent July 1998 benchmark ending 0.02 points lower to yield 3.35 percent at bid.
"They moved along with the money market," one dealer said.
The Dutch central bank is to set a new special advances pact on Thursday and market players wonder if the rate will be hiked some 0.10 or 0.20 points from its current 2.50 percent.
"The guilder weakened further against the mark, but the central bank might just let the weakening continue as long as we don't cross the EMU central rate of 1.1267," one trader said.

Market players are divided about the chances for the bank to hike its rate, as some say it would be a bad sign to markets, while others stress previous unilateral Dutch rate cuts would limit the damage.
